data.name: Settings_ShowButtonText
data.value: Show text on buttons instead of icons

data.name: Settings_ShowButtonTextDescription
data.value: Replace the icons on buttons with a short description of what they do.

data.name: Settings_QueueCutoff
data.value: Stop accepting requests after a set time

data.name: Settings_QueueCutoffDescription
data.value: Refuse new entries once the queue would run past this time, allowing the grace period on top. While a stop request is queued the end time is unknown, so the limit is not applied; use a delay instead if you know how long the pause will be.

data.name: Settings_EndOfNightAudioDescription
data.value: The music that means the ball is over. One file, wherever you keep it: it is not imported and never enters the library. Leave it empty and the button in the queue toolbar stays switched off.

data.name: Settings_EndOfNightMissing
data.value: That file is not there, so the end of the night cannot be played.

data.name: Settings_EndOfNightAtCutoff
data.value: Play it after the last track the end time allowed

data.name: Settings_EndOfNightAtCutoffDescription
data.value: The last thing the room hears is the thing that means go home, without anybody having to press it while packing up. Once it is queued nothing else goes in; removing it reopens the evening.

data.name: Settings_DelayDescription
data.value: Used for 'Request Delay' - pauses playback for this duration

data.name: Settings_PresentationDescription
data.value: Number of presentation windows to show (0 = disabled)

data.name: Settings_AutoQueueDescription
data.value: Automatically adds a random track when playing. Removed when manually adding items.

data.name: Settings_AllowDuplicates
data.value: Allow duplicate tracks in queue in the same session

data.name: Settings_AllowDuplicatesDescription
data.value: When disabled, tracks that are currently playing, in the queue, or have already played this session cannot be added again.

data.name: Settings_ConfirmPlayback
data.value: Confirm before skip, clear, restart, and seek

data.name: Settings_ConfirmPlaybackDescription
data.value: Show a confirmation dialog before skipping to the next item, clearing the current track, restarting playback, or seeking to a different position

data.name: Settings_ThemeDescription
data.value: Choose between Auto (follows system), Light, or Dark theme

data.name: Settings_LanguageDescription
data.value: Application language (requires restart to take effect)

data.name: Settings_ExportLogDescription
data.value: Save the application log file for troubleshooting or bug reports

data.name: Queue_EndOfNightMarker
data.value: END OF THE NIGHT - Nothing follows this

data.name: Queue_EndOfNightMissing

data.name: Queue_PlaylistOpenEnded

data.name: QueueToolbar_EndOfNight
data.value: End the night: queue the closing music, after which nothing else goes in

data.name: Settings_LanguageRestartMessage
data.value: The application needs to restart to apply the new language. Restart now?

data.name: Settings_WebServerEnabled
data.value: Serve the presentation display to a browser

data.name: Settings_WebServerDescription
data.value: Serves the display page, and optionally a phone remote, to any device on the same network: a laptop at the projector, a tablet on a stand, your phone. Off by default; nothing else in the app depends on it.

data.name: Settings_WebRemoteControlDescription
data.value: A separate page that can play, pause, skip and add to the queue. Anyone who can reach it and knows the PIN can change what the room is dancing to, so it is off unless you want it.

data.name: Settings_WebRegeneratePinDescription
data.value: A new PIN disconnects every phone using the old one.

data.name: Wizard_DanceList_Explanation
data.value: Every dance the balfolk scene dances, and every name each one goes by. It comes from BigBalfolkList and is used exactly as published, so there is nothing to answer here: the names in your filenames are matched against it, and it is what a random pick draws from.

data.name: Wizard_Music_Explanation
data.value: Point Ready4Balfolk at the folder your music lives in. Everything below it is included, however it is arranged.

data.name: Wizard_Music_Note
data.value: You can leave this for now and set it in the settings screen later.

data.name: Settings_RunSetupAgainDescription
data.value: Opens the setup wizard. Your dance list and your music folder stay as they are unless you change them there.

data.name: Wizard_DanceList_Detail
data.value: A copy is shipped with the application, so this works with no internet. It is refreshed when Ready4Balfolk starts, and you can ask for a newer one at any time from the dance panel.

data.name: DanceList_UpdateTip
data.value: Fetch the list as BigBalfolkList publishes it right now

data.name: DanceList_UpdateFromFileTip
data.value: Take the list from a dances.json on this computer

data.name: DanceList_Updated
data.value: Dance list updated. {0} dances are new.

data.name: DanceList_AlreadyCurrent
data.value: The dance list was already the published one.

data.name: DanceList_UpdateFailed
data.value: The dance list could not be updated: {0}. The one you have is still in use.

data.name: DanceList_PickThisDance
data.value: Queue a random track of this dance

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Explanation
data.value: This takes a few minutes. Nothing here is permanent: every one of these screens is in the application afterwards, and you can come back to this from the settings whenever you like.

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Stage1Detail
data.value: Every balfolk dance and every name it goes by, published by BigBalfolkList and used as it stands. It is fetched for you, there is nothing to fill in, and it is what your music is matched against.

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Stage2Detail
data.value: One folder. Everything below it counts, however it is arranged, and no particular naming convention is needed.

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Stage3Detail
data.value: Optional. If your files follow a shape, say so once and every file that matches is answered in one act. If they do not, nothing is assumed.

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Source
data.value: The dance list is published at

data.name: Settings_MusicDirectoryChangeHint
data.value: Changing this re-reads your whole library, so it is part of setup rather than a setting on its own.

data.name: Settings_AdvancedDiscoveryHint
data.value: Tell the application how your files are named and arranged. Nothing is assumed about your library until you do.

data.name: Discovery_Intro
data.value: Your library is read as it is found: no folder is assumed to be an artist and no file name is assumed to have fields in it. A rule you state here answers every file it matches in one go, so you are shown what it would do before you add it.

data.name: Discovery_PatternsHint
data.value: %d dance, %a artist, %t title, %n track number, %i ignore, %ex extension. Everything else has to be there exactly. The first pattern that matches a whole name wins, so order them from most specific to least.

data.name: Discovery_Coverage
data.value: Your rules account for {0} of {1} files. {2} are left for you.

data.name: Discovery_ProblemUnknownToken
data.value: That is not one of the tokens.

data.name: Discovery_ProblemNoFields
data.value: This picks out nothing, so it would answer nothing.

data.name: Discovery_ProblemAdjacentFields
data.value: Two fields with nothing between them: where one ends cannot be known.

data.name: Discovery_ProblemDuplicateField
data.value: The same field twice, which cannot both be true.

data.name: Discovery_FoldersHint
data.value: Counted from the outside in. A level only speaks for the files that are actually that deep.

data.name: Discovery_TagsHint
data.value: Which tag fields hold which value in your library. Left alone, artist and album artist are read as the artist, the title tag as the title, and no tag is read as the dance. A dance name from your list is still found in any tag, whatever you set here.

data.name: Discovery_CustomDanceTagHint
data.value: The name of a custom tag in your files whose value is the dance, such as DANCE or STYLE. Leave empty if your files carry no such tag.

data.name: EditTrack_UnknownDance
data.value: The dance list does not know "{0}". A missing dance is a proposal at BigBalfolkList, not a local override.

data.name: Review_Intro
data.value: Nothing is waiting. New files, retagged files and renamed ones come back here on their own.

data.name: Review_Keys
data.value: Tab between the fields, up and down between the tracks. Enter answers one, Shift+Enter the whole folder. Shift+Space listens, Escape stops, and the arrows then skip five seconds. The least certain come first, so stopping early still leaves your library better.

data.name: Review_ReasonUnknownDance
data.value: that dance is not in the list

data.name: Review_ReasonChanged
data.value: the file changed after you answered it

data.name: Review_UnknownDanceHint
data.value: The dance list is shared, so a missing dance is a proposal at BigBalfolkList rather than something to add here. Your answer is kept, and the track goes into the library the moment the list carries the name.

data.name: Wizard_Review_Explanation
data.value: Nothing reaches your library until it has an artist, a title, a dance from the published list, and you agreeing to all three. The least certain come first, so answering the top of the list is worth the most. You can answer these now or leave them: the same screen is in the application, and nothing here has to be finished before you use it.

data.name: Review_Scanning
data.value: Reading your library. {0} tracks so far.

data.name: Review_ScanningHint
data.value: The first time takes a few minutes. Nothing can be answered until it is done, because a queue built from half a library is worse than no queue.

data.name: Wizard_Welcome_Stage4Detail
data.value: Your music is read once, which takes a few minutes the first time. Nothing reaches your library until it has an artist, a title, a dance from the list and your say-so, so whatever is left over waits for you. Answer as much or as little of it as you feel like.

data.name: Wizard_Discovery_Explanation
data.value: Optional, and worth a minute if your files follow a shape. A rule stated here answers every file it matches in one act, so the step after this is the leftovers rather than your whole library. Nothing is assumed if you skip it.

data.name: Discovery_Scanning
data.value: Reading your library. A rule can be measured once that is done.

data.name: Discovery_ApplyHint
data.value: The folder levels and tags above do nothing until you save them. Your library is read again afterwards, so a rule answers the files already in it.

data.name: Review_Preview
data.value: Listen to a bit of this

data.name: Review_PreviewRefused
data.value: The room is listening to the queue, so nothing is played here.

data.name: Review_UsedForAll
data.value: {0} tracks now say {1}. They still want confirming, one by one.

data.name: Review_NotADanceHint
data.value: Clears it everywhere it appears and remembers it, so a rescan does not put it back. The tracks still need a real dance.

data.name: Discovery_ProposalsHint
data.value: Measured from your own files, and applied to nothing until you say so. Where the measurements do not agree, the shape is shown and nothing is named.

data.name: Discovery_ProposalShapeUnnamed
data.value: {0} of {1} files share a shape, and nothing in it can be named

data.name: Discovery_ProposalLevel
data.value: Level {0} looks like the {1}. {2} of {3} agree.

data.name: Discovery_ProposalPosition
data.value: position {0}: {1} - {2} of {5} are dance names, {3} different values, {4} agree with a tag

data.name: Review_RulesHint
data.value: How your files are named. A rule here empties this queue in one go.

data.name: Review_AllowOutsideTheList
data.value: Let dances outside the published list into my library

data.name: Review_AllowOutsideTheListHint
data.value: Off, a dance the list does not carry keeps its track here until a proposal at BigBalfolkList is merged. On, your answer is enough - but a random pick draws by tag, and a dance nobody has published has none, so those tracks never come up on their own.

data.name: Review_ApproveFolderConfirm
data.value: This answers {0} tracks in {1}, taking the artist and title each one already has. Nothing is filled in for you, and a track still missing something is left alone.

data.name: Discovery_DanceListHint
data.value: The dance list every track is matched against. It is shared, so a dance missing from it is proposed there rather than added here, and your tracks waiting on one go into your library the moment it carries the name.
